classes.ownership_argument: Each chunk owns its maxima/sum and exponential interval. Probability stage owns one index. Strict rank with lower-index tie break gives a unique writer for each admitted rank, its probability, and its two triples. The final probability normalization has one work-item.

Each descriptor index and each repeated-row output index has one writer. Invalid-ID flags are stored independently; one later work-item raises sticky error, after deterministic safe descriptor/data initialization.
Each chunk writes one candidate and one invalid flag; the second stage is one work-item. Bad-value fallback runs serially and writes the result before setting error.

Stage zero writes one subtree partial per row/chunk. Stage one reads completed partials and owns four output positions. In-place combined streams are read and written by the same output owner; norm_value never reads another output position. Branch/injection/gain inputs must remain distinct from norm outputs, as in the plan.

Each work-item owns one (head,value-coordinate) state row of 128 elements and all token outputs at that coordinate. The token loop within that owner serializes recurrence. Stage-zero query/key ranges and 48 decay/beta slots are disjoint.
Each row/chunk owns one partial; second-stage four-coordinate output tiles are disjoint. RoPE partner reads read-only input values, not other work-items output.

Current-token cache writes do not intersect previous-token cache reads (r < position). New-token pooled reads use the input row, not the concurrently appended cache. Partial sums and pooled output tiles have distinct owners.

First stage initializes each selection output and one score per block. Second-stage rank uniqueness makes rank*4 output ranges disjoint; the one trailing-token writer starts after selected full blocks.

Score owns one head/slot; softmax phases write disjoint max/sum/exponential/normalized spans separated by queue order; value owns one output/chunk partial then one final output coordinate. No cross-work-item communication lacks a kernel boundary.

Dedicated SimpleNew<hc_mix,0> broadcast instantiation assigns exactly one work-item to each output index. It reads index modulo the immutable source-row extent. The registered streams output is distinct from its embedding input; no writer modifies the shared source row.

Dedicated SimpleNew<ple_add,0> assigns one writer per output index and reads the three inputs at that same index. The intermediate addition is rounded before the outer addition. The registered in-place streams alias is safe because no work-item reads another work-item output coordinate.

The host selects 2560-width/four-head norm and combine specializations only after matching those exact dimensions; route512/top10 likewise matches before dispatch. Template constants replace the same admitted shape fields and do not change work-item count or partition boundaries.

For rows-per-group R and split S, subgroup row rr, projection p and split part have local slot (2*rr+p)*S+part, written by lane0 alone. Local size has R*S subgroups. A workgroup barrier precedes reads by lane0/part0, the sole writer of each global slot*rows+row. Only row0/part0/lane0 writes each route status. Active and route-valid predicates are subgroup-uniform. Paired projection buffers must be distinct as in registered plans; arbitrary adversarial aliases remain outside this review.

guard_review: Sticky error uses device-scope atomic load/store on native paths. Invalid routes can leave internal scratch partially written in a schedule-dependent manner; subsequent kernels observe sticky error and do not commit semantic outputs. Gather defers error until initialization is complete. No data race was found in visible output writes. This is not a claim that arbitrary scratch bytes are deterministic.
ordering_review: specialised_submit creates separate submissions for every stage. Device chains them, and tp2 Context omits explicit native dependencies only after same-card validation on an in-order queue. Card changes and all peer copies retain host drain+retirement fences.
limits: Static review does not prove hardware execution ordering; K1 two fresh owners plus randomized CPU scheduling are mandatory.
Valid registered bindings are assumed; arbitrary adversarial output/input aliasing beyond the plan is not supported.
Core kernel and packet18 reference remain independent CPU/device exactness comparators.
scope: Final source-only read-through of registered specialised kernel write ownership, fixed-shape dispatch and packet25 bridge; no device execution or new test run by this reviewer.
bridge_addendum: review-bridge-addendum.md independently records the final bridge admission/bit-identity review by the windows subagent. This reviewer additionally read its final source and independently checked scratch, output and status write ownership.
